text: The RFP seeks implementation and integration of Oracle ERP and Utility Billing solutions

citations.text: The purpose of this request for proposal (RFP) is to invite qualified implementation partners to submit a proposal for the deployment and integration of Oracle's Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and Utility Billing solutions for the City of Durham in North Carolina (the City).
This RFP focuses exclusively on seeking a partner for the implementation phase.

text: The City’s goal is to integrate business processes and provide consistent corporate data across Finance, Budget and Management Services, Customer Billing Services, and Human Resources

text: The City needs to replace fragmented systems and manual processes that limit reporting, data visibility, and decision-making

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: The City operates in an environment of largely unintegrated disparate systems, some of which are unsupported and lack reporting capabilities.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: The City operates through a significant amount of manual interaction from users across the entire organization.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: The existing ecosystem of applications (and supporting environment of manual tools) are not sufficient to support the needed business capabilities.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: As expectations from the business and residents increase, the absence of a single source of truth is emerging as a major challenge.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: Multiple systems of record, along with other departments’ local solutions, create an operating environment rampant with inefficiency and manual activity that can inhibit process effectiveness.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Multiple systems of record resulting in the duplication of data, complicating data availability, cross checking, and reporting.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Manual processes and lack of visibility into disparate systems creating inconsistent information.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Time-consuming data reconciliation processes and lack of visibility into disparate systems, creating inconsistent answers to the same questions.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • The inability to make data-driven business decisions due to the absence of aggregate data from a single integrated, reliable set of information.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Increased resource effort spent on non-value-added functions (e.g., re-keying, data validation, tracing transactions).

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • Individual departments operating with different systems, which contribute to a lack of coordination and cohesion between the departments.

citations.section: 2.3. Major drivers for Enterprise Resource Planning
citations.text: • A recognition that operationally, the existing tools may be a barrier to scalability and future operations.

text: The City seeks a partner experienced in local government Oracle ERP implementation, including utility billing, customer accounts, meter reading, and billing processes

citations.text: The City requires a partner with proven expertise in effectively implementing Oracle's solutions, particularly in areas critical to local government operations such as utility billing (including customer accounts management, meter reading, and customer billing processes).
The ideal Proponent must have experience in successfully implementing the Oracle ERP solution within a local government environment.

text: The City’s partner-selection factors include state and city implementation experience, Oracle ERP experience, collaboration, communication, support, methodology, viability, capability, references, cooperation, and price

citations.text: The City's Partner selection decision will be based on Partner’s competency evaluated across a number of factors.

Factors to be considered include State/City Implementation Experience, Oracle ERP Solution Implementation experience, Collaboration, Communication & Support, Implementation Methodology, Proponent viability, Proponent capability, customer references, willingness to work cooperatively, and overall price.

text: The City has selected Oracle as its enterprise software solution; this solicitation is for implementation services only

citations.text: This solicitation represents the second phase of a two-step process.
The first phase involved the selection of Oracle as the Enterprise software solution.
This RFP focuses exclusively on seeking a partner for the implementation phase.

text: The City engaged Info-Tech Research Group Inc. to support its ERP implementation process

citations.text: The City, in collaboration with Info-Tech Research Group Inc (Info-Tech), is now advancing to the next critical phase of its enterprise solution journey – the implementation of the selected Oracle solution.

This process, integral to the successful deployment of the ERP and Utility Billing solutions, will be conducted through a structured and collaborative approach, adhering to the proven Info-Tech methodology for ERP Implementation projects.
